issues.description: revoke_error exposed via API may leak sensitive backend details
issues.detail: vault/logical_system.go now surfaces leaseInfo.RevokeErr verbatim in the lease lookup response. Revoke errors from backends frequently include URLs, principal names, DB hostnames, or upstream error strings. The PR description itself flags this concern but ships without a redaction policy or capability gate. Consider gating behind sudo or sanitizing the message before returning to API callers.

issues.description: Schema declares 'path' Required but response omits it when empty
issues.detail: logical_system_paths.go marks 'path' as Required: true, but handleLeaseLookup always sets resp.Data["path"] = leaseInfo.Path even when empty string. If leaseInfo.Path is ever empty (e.g. malformed entry), the response still satisfies the required-field contract, but namespace_path/revoke_error are correctly optional. Verify token-auth leases populate Path; otherwise mark schema accordingly.

issues.description: Renamed exported API breaks downstream consumers of FetchLeaseTimes
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is a public method on ExpirationManager and was renamed to FetchLeaseInfo without a deprecation shim. Any external code or plugins importing vault as a library will fail to compile. Consider keeping FetchLeaseTimes as a thin wrapper calling FetchLeaseInfo and marking it deprecated.

issues.description: Unrelated context change mixed into rename test
issues.detail: In TestExpiration_revokeEntry_rejected_fairsharing the call was changed from namespace.RootContext(nil) to namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) alongside the rename, while the sibling test TestExpiration_FetchLeaseTimesIrrevocable keeps nil. The inconsistency is confusing; either apply t.Context() consistently or revert to nil to keep this diff minimal.

issues.description: Test coverage missing for namespace_path and revoke_error fields
issues.detail: logical_system_test.go only asserts the new 'path' field. No test exercises namespace_path population (requires non-root namespace) or revoke_error surfacing (requires a failed revocation). Given the security sensitivity called out in the PR description, adding at minimum a revoke_error assertion would be valuable.

FetchLeaseInfo still emits metrics.MeasureSince with the key 'expire.fetch-lease-times'. This is acceptable for backward-compatible dashboards but worth a comment explaining the intentional mismatch with the new function name, otherwise future readers may 'fix' it and break monitoring.

review.summary: This PR usefully extends the lease lookup response with path, namespace_path, and revoke_error, and refactors FetchLeaseTimes into FetchLeaseInfo. The main concern is the unconditional exposure of RevokeErr, which the author themselves flagged as a possible information-leak vector; it should be gated or sanitized before merge. The public rename also risks breaking downstream consumers without a deprecation shim. Tests cover the new path field but omit namespace_path and revoke_error scenarios.
